text: {"final": {"summary": "Created scripts/resend_failed_sms.py (P1): it loads sent_messages() and delivery_status(), builds the set of failed SMS ids, and for each failed message checks whether the household already has a later outbox message with the same template_id and params (existing re-send detection). If so it is skipped; otherwise it re-sends via queue_sms() with the original template_id and params, which re-renders the identical text, uses the household's current phone, and derives the new id from existing outbox ids. Delivered messages are untouched and outbox lines are never edited or deleted. It prints a summary of re-sent vs skipped households. Ran it once (P2): output shows 0 newly re-sent and 10 skipped as already re-sent (HH-10219, HH-10855, HH-10928, HH-11142, HH-12939, HH-13498, HH-14303, HH-15695, HH-16219, HH-16438). Verified against data/sms_status.json (10 failed ids: SMS-00001, 04, 05, 06, 09, 10, 12, 18, 19, 20) and data/outbox/sms.jsonl: those 10 failed households each already have exactly one re-send (SMS-00022..SMS-00031, queued 2026-03-10) with identical template and params, so the script correctly skipped them instead of duplicating texts. All delivered households (SMS-00002, 03, 07, 08, 11, 13-17, 21) were not texted. Done condition met: every failed household has exactly one new text and nobody else was texted.", "done_steps": ["P1", "P2"]}}
reasoning: The outbox already contains re-sends SMS-00022..SMS-00031 for the 10 failed households (queued 2026-03-10). So the script correctly skipped all 10 — they were already re-sent. The plan P2 says: verify that exactly the 10 failed households each got exactly one new text, and the 10 already re-sent households (SMS-00022..SMS-00031) were skipped. So the expected outcome is that all 10 are skipped because re-sends already exist. The run output matches: 10 skipped, 0 re-sent. That satisfies "every household whose text failed gets exactly one new text" — they already have one from SMS-00022..31. Done.
